facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer already sells an object-proximity warning system for machines used in construction, mining, quarrying and similar work.
facts.quote: already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: It is now developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the heavy off-road automatic braking system arrive in mid-2027; validation must then finish in under four months.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in under four months.

facts.text: Historically, validating this kind of heavy off-road machine function took three to four years, mostly through physical testing and tuning for each machine model.
facts.quote: In the past, validating a function of this kind took three to four years, mostly through physical testing and tuning for each machine model.

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than 100 types of job site.
facts.quote: The new system must work across more than 100 types of job site

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than ten operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: more than ten operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work in many weather and light conditions, including rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: many weather and light conditions (rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness, glare)

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.
facts.quote: many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.

facts.text: The sensor set for the heavy off-road automatic braking system is not yet confirmed.
facts.quote: The sensor set is not yet confirmed

facts.text: Because the heavy off-road automatic braking system's sensor set is unconfirmed, the research had to cover camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other sensor options.
facts.quote: The sensor set is not yet confirmed, so camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options all had to be covered.

facts.text: The research sought real cases where collision warning or automatic braking functions were validated with much less physical testing than before, including realistic timelines, results and failures.
facts.quote: The goal of the research was to find real cases where a collision warning or automatic braking function was validated with much less physical testing than before, and to report realistic timelines, results and failures.

facts.text: Skeptical reviewers ask first for real-case evidence of collision warning or automatic braking validation with substantially reduced physical testing.
facts.quote: Skeptical reviewers ask for this evidence first.

facts.text: The research sought documented validation cases in passenger cars, trucks and buses, mining, construction, agriculture, forestry, forklifts and warehouse vehicles, port equipment, rail, aviation and military ground vehicles.
facts.quote: Find documented cases in passenger cars, trucks and buses, mining, construction, agriculture, forestry, forklifts and warehouse vehicles, port equipment, rail, aviation and military ground vehicles.

facts.text: For each validation precedent, the research sought what was validated, the methods used, capability-building time, validation time, remaining physical testing and who accepted the evidence: a regulator, customer or internal safety board.
facts.quote: For each case: what was validated, which methods were used, how long it took to build the capability, how long validation then took, how much physical testing remained, and who accepted the evidence (regulator, customer or internal safety board).

facts.text: The research sought failed or delayed validation efforts and their causes, including recalls, investigations and field problems linked to weak validation, such as unnecessary automatic braking.
facts.quote: Which efforts failed or were delayed, and why, including recalls, investigations or field problems linked to weak validation, such as unnecessary automatic braking.

facts.text: The research sought the typical time needed for an organization new to virtual validation to build a usable capability, along with the required team size and skills.
facts.quote: How long an organization new to this typically needs to build a usable virtual validation capability, and what team size and skills it took.

facts.text: The research sought off-road machine makers already selling automatic braking systems and their published limits on speed range, direction of travel, object types and conditions.
facts.quote: Which makers of off-road machines already sell systems that brake automatically, and what limits they publish (speed range, direction of travel, object types, conditions).

facts.text: The research sought whether standards bodies or industry groups had studied applying on-road simulation methods to off-road machines, and their conclusions.
facts.quote: Whether any standards body or industry group has studied the use of on-road simulation methods for off-road machines, and what it concluded.

facts.text: The research was required to remain neutral across vendors, products and technologies.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral across vendors, products and technologies

facts.text: The research was required to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.
facts.quote: to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.

facts.text: Each important research claim was to be labeled as independent evidence (an independent study, standard or third-party test), the vendor's own claim, or expert opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labeled by evidence type (independent study, standard or third-party test; the vendor's own claim; or expert opinion)

facts.text: Every research source was to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for tools and products.
facts.quote: every source was to be dated, with a preference for 2023 or later for tools and products.

facts.text: The research was required to report failures, limits and evidence against each approach, not only successes.
facts.quote: Failures, limits and evidence against each approach were to be reported, not only successes.

facts.text: The research was required to mark evidence proven only for on-road vehicles as on-road-only evidence.
facts.quote: Anything proven only for on-road vehicles was to be marked as such

facts.text: When the research could find no evidence, the answer was required to be “not found” rather than a guess.
facts.quote: where nothing could be found the answer was to be "not found" rather than a guess.
